knowledge:
- key_parameters: scale=Controls row scaling in genefinder; options are "none", "range" (scales to 0-1 interval), or "zscore" (standardizes using mean and standard deviation) ;; method=Distance measure in genefinder; options include "euclidean", "maximum", "manhattan", "canberra", and "binary" ;; kOverA=Non-specific filter function where the first argument is the minimum number of samples and the second is the minimum expression threshold ;; ttest=Specific filter function wrapper around t.test where the first argument is the covariate factor and p is the p-value significance threshold ;; theta=A numeric vector of quantiles between 0 and 1 specifying the filtering fractions for independent filtering diagnostics in filtered_p and filtered_R
- alternatives: geneplotter=Mentioned for visualizing gene expression data ;; annotate=Mentioned for downstream exploration of filtered gene lists, such as searching PubMed abstracts or downloading sequence information ;; class=The knn function from this package is used for k-nearest neighbor classification in cross-validation workflows
- when_to_use: Use when you need to filter out uninformative genes (non-specific filtering) or non-differentially expressed genes (specific filtering) from high-throughput expression datasets to reduce dimensionality before downstream analysis. Also use when you want to find genes with similar expression profiles to a set of target genes, or when optimizing independent filtering thresholds to maximize statistical power.
- pitfalls: Failing to scale rows (using scale="none") in genefinder when genes have different baseline expression levels, which can lead to distance metrics being dominated by absolute expression magnitude rather than profile shape ;; Using Canberra distance (method="canberra") when data contains zero values, as terms with zero numerator and denominator are omitted and treated as missing ;; Applying specific filters (e.g., t-test based on sample groups) before cross-validation, which can cause selection bias (the documentation demonstrates correct nested gene selection within a cross-validation loop to avoid this)

workflows.name: gene_filtering
workflows.intent: Filter genes from an expression dataset using non-specific criteria, specific criteria, or a combination of both.
input: sample.ExpressionSet (ExpressionSet containing expression data and sample covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the dataset and packages ;; 2. Define a non-specific filter using kOverA ;; 3. Define a specific filter using ttest ;; 4. Combine the filters using filterfun ;; 5. Apply the filters to the expression matrix using genefilter
workflows.code:
library("Biobase")
library("genefilter")
data(sample.ExpressionSet)
f1 <- kOverA(5, 200)
ffun <- filterfun(f1)
wh1 <- genefilter(exprs(sample.ExpressionSet), ffun)
sum(wh1)
f2 <- ttest(sample.ExpressionSet$type, p=0.1)
wh2 <- genefilter(exprs(sample.ExpressionSet), filterfun(f2))
sum(wh2)
ffun_combined <- filterfun(f1, f2)
wh3 <- genefilter(exprs(sample.ExpressionSet), ffun_combined)
sum(wh3)

workflows.name: gene_finding
workflows.intent: Find genes with expression profiles most similar to a set of target genes of interest.
workflows.stages: 1. Define the indices of the target genes of interest ;; 2. Run genefinder to identify the nearest neighbor genes using a specified distance metric and scaling method ;; 3. Extract the indices and distances of the nearest genes ;; 4. Retrieve the feature names of the identified neighbor genes
workflows.code:
library("Biobase")
library("genefilter")
data(sample.ExpressionSet)
igenes <- c(300,333,355,419)
closeg <- genefinder(sample.ExpressionSet, igenes, 10, method="euc", scale="none")
names(closeg)
closeg$"31539_r_at"
Nms1 <- featureNames(sample.ExpressionSet)[closeg$"31539_r_at"$indices]
Nms1

workflows.name: independent_filtering_diagnostics
workflows.intent: Optimize the independent filtering threshold to maximize the number of discoveries while controlling the false discovery rate.
input: ALL (ExpressionSet containing gene expression data and phenotypic covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Subset the dataset to relevant samples ;; 2. Compute a filter statistic (row variances) and unadjusted p-values (row t-tests) ;; 3. Compute adjusted p-values across a range of filtering thresholds (theta) using filtered_p ;; 4. Visualize the number of rejections across thresholds using rejection_plot ;; 5. Calculate the exact number of rejections at a given alpha level across thresholds using filtered_R and plot the results
workflows.code:
library("genefilter")
library("ALL")
data("ALL")
bcell <- grep("^B", as.character(ALL$BT))
moltyp <- which(as.character(ALL$mol.biol) %in% 
                c("NEG", "BCR/ABL"))
ALL_bcrneg <- ALL[, intersect(bcell, moltyp)]
ALL_bcrneg$mol.biol <- factor(ALL_bcrneg$mol.biol)
S2 <- rowVars(exprs(ALL_bcrneg))
p2 <- rowttests(ALL_bcrneg, "mol.biol")$p.value
theta <- seq(0, .5, .1)
p_bh <- filtered_p(S2, p2, theta, method="BH")
head(p_bh)
rejection_plot(p_bh, at="sample",
               xlim=c(0,.3), ylim=c(0,1000),
               main="Benjamini & Hochberg adjustment")
theta <- seq(0, .80, .01)
R_BH <- filtered_R(alpha=.10, S2, p2, theta, method="BH")
head(R_BH)
plot(theta, R_BH, type="l",
     xlab=expression(theta), ylab="Rejections",
     main="BH cutoff = 0.1")
